messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 502s observed in northeast edge pool (ne1-edge). Aggregated error rate 18% over last 3m. Automatically triggered severity P2.
Ryan (on-call): I'm up — looking. Any customer reports yet?
Support Liaison: A support ticket just popped for customer 'GreenCargo' reporting timeouts, CS is triaging. No broad customer outage reported so far.
Sara M: Confirming dashboards — frontend gateway 502 spike started ~10:54 UTC, spike aligns with mlworker saturations in ne1-a.
Alex C: Checking worker pool — current pod restarts skewing. `kubectl get pods -n mlworkers -l region=ne1 -o wide` shows 6/18 in CrashLoopBackOff.
Cheng: Logs show `error: upstream read timeout` from proxy to mlworker: `upstream_read_timeout while reading response header from upstream` repeating.
Priya K: Can we scale the mlworker pool and drain the bad nodes? Suggest bumping replicas to 36 and cordon the autoscaling group instances with high OOMs.
Ryan (on-call): Proceed with controlled scale. Alex, run scale and tag the deploy for roll-back potential.
Alex C: Running:
```
kubectl scale deploy/mlworker --replicas=36 -n mlworkers
kubectl rollout status deploy/mlworker -n mlworkers --timeout=4m
```
Alex C: Also patching readinessProbe to be slightly more lenient while we stabilize.
InfraBot: Autoscaler detected instance ne1-bc-03 has repeated OOM, added to eviction list.
Cheng: Noticed a config mismatch — proxy keepalive timeout lowered accidentally in last config push: `proxy_read_timeout=15s` vs expected 60s. That would explain upstream truncation under high tail latency.
Priya K: Rolling back that specific config on the edge proxy for ne1. Command:
```
kubectl apply -f configs/proxy/ne1/keepalive-rollback.yaml
```
Support Liaison: CS updated GreenCargo: "We're investigating elevated errors in NE region; traffic being routed to adjacent regions where possible. We'll update in 15m." :phone: 
Ryan (on-call): Initiating traffic steering to fallback region eu1 for new sessions while ne1 recovers. Applying policy to gateway route table.
Sara M: Adding temporary rule to prefer fallback pool:
```
redwood route update --region us-east --prefer eu1 --matcher "session:new" --duration 15m
```
Cheng: After scale and proxy rollback, error rate dropped to ~4% within 90s — still above baseline but improving.
Alex C: Rolling restart on remaining mlworker pods with `kubectl rollout restart` to clear bad state.
IncidentBot: Action checklist attached: scale mlworkers, rollback proxy timeout, route steer to eu1, notify CS. :white_check_mark: 
Priya K: I'm marking the suspected root cause as 'misapplied proxy timeout + worker instability' pending post-incident analysis.
Ryan (on-call): Who's owning the postmortem? Sara, could you lead the RCA and include timeline + config diff? Tag infra for ASG instance health.
Sara M: I'll lead, will gather logs, config commits, and pod events. Draft will be ready in 24h.
Support Liaison: Communications: prepare an incident note for affected customers and an internal blameless summary. I can draft the customer note once we have definitive timeline.
Cheng: Adding a quick hotfix to default to conservative proxy_read_timeout for all edge configs via CI: `ci/config/edge/defaults`.
Alex C: Observability notes — captured heap/dump from one worker, push to s3 `s3://redwood-ops/ne1/heapdumps/1766000000/` for offline analysis.
Ryan (on-call): Monitoring escalations: if 5xx > 5% for 10m we'll re-open P1 and start cross-org pager. For now status: P2 degraded, mitigation in flight.
IncidentBot: Incident status updated: P2 -> mitigated (partial). Error rate trending down. Autoclose timer 30m.
Support Liaison: CS will follow up with impacted accounts. GreenCargo wants ETA for full recovery; reply with ~1h and flag for SLA credit assessment.
Sara M: Putting follow-up tasks in the incident board: config review, autoscaler tuning, ASG healthcheck improvements, CI defaults, and customer comms.
Ryan (on-call): Thanks all. I'll handoff to day oncall in 45m. Please leave notes in the thread and ping me if it regresses. :thumbsup:
